title: Time, expenses and rates
summary: Captures every billable minute and dollar on a matter. The agent rebuilds the day from email, documents, calendar, calls and its own work, then proposes entries and disbursements with narratives. Nothing becomes billable until the timekeeper accepts it (G9). Rates, fee arrangements, write-downs, timesheet approval and utilization reports sit on top of the accepted record.

screens.agent: Reads the user's activity stream (filed emails, document edits, calendar, call logs, its own runs on the user's behalf), clusters by matter and time, estimates durations, drafts narratives in the firm's style, checks against existing entries to avoid double counting, and flags block billing. Builds suggestions from the passive activity ledger (documents, email, calls, calendar, agent work), cites the source events per entry and writes the narrative in the firm's billing style.
screens.gate: G9: the timekeeper personally accepts each entry (or an explicit unflagged batch) before it is billable. Agent-performed work is never billed as lawyer time unless the firm's fee arrangement says so and the lawyer accepts.
states: expired (older than firm limit, needs supervisor)
edge: email touches two matters: propose a split, not a guess
calendar event with no attendance evidence: low confidence
activity on a matter the user is walled from: never surfaced
agent's own compute time: shown as 'agent work', default non-billable
user on leave: suggestions held, not expired
screens.reg: RPC 3.6-1 and commentary: no billing for time not spent; the lawyer remains responsible for AI-assisted work (RPC 3.1 competence, 6.1 supervision). Billing for time saved by automation as if done by hand may be unfair (verify LSO guidance on AI and fees).

open_questions: Should agent work (drafting done by the agent) ever be billable, and if so as a flat 'technology-assisted' line or as reviewed lawyer time?
Is weekly timesheet approval on by default, or only for staff and students?
Default rounding: 0.1h (6 min) for everyone, or firm-chosen?
Which time signals are allowed by default (email, documents, calendar, calls)? Per-user opt-in needed for privacy?
Do we track time on flat-fee and contingency matters by default (non-billable) for assessment and profitability?
Is a soft-cost markup (photocopies, postage) allowed in the product at all?
Do suggestions expire if not reviewed (e.g. after 14 days), and who handles expired ones?
Need a tax adviser to confirm the agency/own-cost table for common Ontario disbursements before launch.
Do we support UTBMS/LEDES coding in v1, or only for firms with insurer clients?
Is a time lock date (no edits before date X) required, or is 'locked once billed' enough?
Could: firm and personal text snippets (abbreviation to phrase) in narrative fields?
Could: expense report columns naming agent disbursements vs firm cost recovery?
Activity ledger: does Ontario's written electronic monitoring policy rule (ESA) apply to small firms under 25 employees? (verify)
